title: The Wright Flyer fabric on Mars
hook: The first aircraft to fly on Mars carried a scrap of the Wright brothers' plane.
peek: When NASA's Ingenuity helicopter made the first powered flight on another planet in 2021, a stamp-sized piece of fabric from the 1903 Wright Flyer was tucked on board. Two firsts in flight, 118 years apart, travelled together.
lede: On 19 April 2021, NASA's small Ingenuity helicopter rose about 3 metres above Jezero Crater, hovered and landed. It was the first powered, controlled flight on another planet. Beneath its solar panel, wrapped around a cable, was a piece of muslin about the size of a postage stamp, cut from the wing of the Wright brothers' 1903 Flyer.

bullets.text: The fabric came from Carillon Historical Park in Dayton, Ohio, the Wrights' home town, with the support of the Wright family. It was a bottom-left wing fabric from the plane that flew at Kitty Hawk.

NASA named the patch of Jezero Crater where Ingenuity first flew Wright Brothers Field. The UN's civil aviation agency, ICAO, gave it an airfield code, JZRO, and gave Ingenuity a type designation, IGY.
Mars's air is about 1% as dense as Earth's, so the 1.8 kilogram helicopter spun its two rotors at about 2,400 turns a minute, far faster than a helicopter on Earth would need.
Ingenuity was meant as a test of five flights. It ended up flying 72 times over almost three years, until a damaged rotor blade grounded it in January 2024.
It was not the first trip into space for the Flyer. Neil Armstrong carried a piece of its wood and fabric to the Moon on Apollo 11 in 1969.
